chapters.1.lds: The lesson asks readers to consider whether their offerings show honor for God. Why does God compare the offerings with gifts presented to a governor?
chapters.1.summary: The LORD tells Israel that he has loved them, and they ask how. He points to his choice of Jacob over Esau. A son honors his father, yet the priests despise God’s name. They ask how they have done so. They offer blind, lame, and sick animals on his altar. God tells them to try giving such gifts to their governor. He would rather the temple doors were shut. His name will be great among the nations.
chapters.2.lds: The lesson uses the complaint about justice to examine attitudes during difficult times. Why can tears at the altar fail to answer betrayal of a spouse?
chapters.2.summary: God warns the priests that he will curse their blessings. His covenant with Levi was one of life and peace. A priest’s lips should guard knowledge. These priests have caused many to stumble. The people are also faithless to one another. They weep at the altar because God ignores their offerings. The LORD is witness between each man and the wife of his youth. They have wearied him by asking where the God of justice is.
chapters.3.lds: The lesson connects tithing with faith and returning to God. Whose injuries does the judgment name when it answers demands for justice?
chapters.3.summary: God says he is sending a messenger to prepare his way. The Lord they seek will come suddenly to his temple. He will be like a refiner’s fire and will purify the Levites. He will come near to judge. He will testify against those who cheat workers and oppress widows, orphans, and foreigners. He calls the people to return and stop robbing him of tithes. Some say it is useless to serve God. Those who fear the LORD are written in a book of remembrance.
chapters.4.lds: The lesson reads Elijah’s promise through Moroni’s quotation and the later Kirtland Temple account. Why does the final promise concern changed hearts between parents and children?
chapters.4.summary: A day is coming that will burn like a furnace. The proud and the wicked will be like stubble. For those who fear God’s name, the sun of righteousness will rise with healing. They will go out leaping like calves from the stall. The people are told to remember the law of Moses. God will send Elijah the prophet before that great day. He will turn the hearts of fathers to their children. He will turn the hearts of children to their fathers.
